tagline: The old stage road over the mountains to Santa Barbara.
intro: Highway 154 leaves US 101 at Los Olivos, a town named for a ranch of five thousand olive trees, and runs southeast past Santa Ynez and along Cachuma Lake into Los Padres National Forest. It crosses the Santa Ynez Mountains at San Marcos Pass, never much above 2,000 feet, and comes down the other side to Santa Barbara.

Before US 101 went through Gaviota Pass this was the main road to Santa Barbara, and a stagecoach route in its early years. Frémont's battalion came over the pass on a rainy Christmas Eve in 1846, when it was only a rough path, and lost 150 horses and mules sliding down the mud.

moments.title: Cachuma Lake
moments.text: The Santa Ynez River backs up behind Bradbury Dam beside the road, a reservoir that fell to about 7 percent of capacity in 2016 and was nearly full again in January 2023.

moments.title: Cold Spring Canyon Arch Bridge
moments.text: The highway crosses Cold Spring Canyon on a steel arch opened in 1964, its deck 400 feet above the canyon floor.

moments.title: Cold Spring Tavern
moments.text: Down in the canyon on the old stage road, a relay station of 1865 was in 1956 the first restaurant to serve the Hensons' guest-ranch salad dressing, since known as ranch.

practical: Caltrans and the California Highway Patrol have designated the road over San Marcos Pass a daylight-headlight highway because of frequent accidents.
